record.paper_title: Billiard Dynamics: A Survey with the Emphasis on Open Problems
record.context_brief: Counting periodic bands in irrational polygons
record.original_question: For an irrational polygon P, let f_P(ℓ) denote the number of periodic bands of billiard orbits of length at most ℓ. Find nontrivial upper and lower bounds for f_P(ℓ).

evidence.quote: Denote by fP(ℓ) the number of periodic bands of length at most ℓ. This is a counting function of periodic orbits in polygons.
Problem 11. Find nontrivial (upper and lower) bounds on fP for irrational polygons.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a simple polygon. The billiard flow in $P$ is the dynamical system describing a point particle moving in straight lines inside $P$ and reflecting elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) off the sides; trajectories meeting a vertex are undefined.

Call $P$ irrational if at least one interior angle of $P$ is an irrational multiple of $\pi$.

A periodic billiard orbit in $P$ is a closed billiard trajectory. Any periodic orbit which does not hit a vertex belongs to a maximal one-parameter family of parallel periodic orbits of equal length, called a periodic band. The length $\ell(B)$ of a periodic band $B$ is defined as the common length of the trajectories composing $B$.

For $\ell > 0$, define
$$f_P(\ell) = \#\{B : B \text{ is a periodic band in } P \text{ with } \ell(B) \le \ell\}.$$

Problem: For an arbitrary irrational polygon $P$, establish nontrivial upper and lower bounds (as $\ell \to \infty$) for the counting function $f_P(\ell)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is widely regarded as open. Partial results exist: Troubetzkoy and others have established superlinear lower bounds (of the form $n (\log n)^k$) for open sets of irrational polygons, but no general nontrivial upper bound and no matching lower bound for arbitrary irrational polygons is known. Surveys (e.g., Schwartz's ICM lecture; Masur–Tabachnikov's handbook chapter on rational billiards) emphasize that the counting problem for irrational polygons remains essentially unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Lower bounds on growth rates of periodic billiard trajectories in some irrational polygons
status_evidence.snippet: There is an open set of polygons (with a fixed number of sides) for which the number of periodic billiard paths of length at most n grows faster than n log^k n.
status_evidence.claim: Superlinear lower bounds are known for some irrational polygons, but not general matching bounds.

status_evidence.title: Survey Lecture on Billiards (R. E. Schwartz)
status_evidence.snippet: Very little is known about billiards in irrational polygons, including counting of periodic orbits.
status_evidence.claim: The counting problem for irrational polygons is largely open.

status_evidence.title: Rational billiards and flat structures (Masur–Tabachnikov)
status_evidence.snippet: Counting generalized diagonals and periodic orbits is a classical problem; the irrational case is poorly understood compared to the rational case.
status_evidence.claim: No general nontrivial bounds for f_P in the irrational case are established.
